title: Can radial arms give exactly five or six angles of symmetry?
description: Five equal radial arms and then six equal radial arms are placed round a dot, and the full turn is shared between the gaps. The turns that fit are listed by repeating the gap up to the full turn. Keeko's doubt is that any five arms give five angles of symmetry, whatever the gaps.
teaching_notes: One idea: n equal arms with equal gaps give n angles of symmetry, and each gap is three hundred sixty divided by n. Watch for students who think the gaps do not matter.

source: Can you draw a figure with radial arms that has a) exactly 5
video_script.why: The child draws radial-arm figures with exactly five and exactly six angles of symmetry and lists the angles.
video_script.substitution: five and then six equal radial arms round a dot, the way the book draws radial arms
video_script.anchor: equal radial arms round a dot, drawn the way the book draws radial arms
video_script.wrong_answer: any five arms give five angles of symmetry
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko draws five arms with uneven gaps and expects five angles of symmetry.
video_script.payoff_line: Five equal arms and six equal arms both work

final_answer.spoken: yes, five equal arms seventy two degrees apart, and six equal arms sixty degrees apart

maths_rules: n equal arms with equal gaps give n angles of symmetry, and the gap is 360 ÷ n
uneven gaps leave only the full turn
video_script.design: Five equal arms round a dot, then six equal arms. The gap is found from the full turn, and the turns that fit are written one after another. Keeko's doubt is that any five arms will do.

marks.three: three equal arms appear with 120° between them

<bookmark mark='three'/>Three equal arms are one hundred twenty degrees apart.
Each gap is the full turn, shared equally.
<bookmark mark='name'/>A turn after which the figure looks the same is called an angle of symmetry.

beats.on_screen: Given: a figure with radial arms; exactly 5 angles of symmetry, then exactly 6
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a figure with radial arms.
It must have exactly five angles of symmetry, and then exactly six.

beats.on_screen: To find: the arms that work, and the angles of symmetry
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the arms that work.
We also list the angles of symmetry.

beats.on_screen: n equal arms, equal gaps: gap = 360° ÷ n; use 5 arms for 5 angles

marks.rule: the rule gap = 360° ÷ number of arms is written
marks.five: five equal arms appear round the dot

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, use as many equal arms as angles of symmetry.
Each gap is three hundred sixty degrees divided by the number of arms.
<bookmark mark='five'/>For five angles, draw five equal arms.

marks.list: the five turns are written one after the other
marks.sum: the first three turns are ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>Step two, three hundred sixty divided by five is seventy two degrees.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Repeat that gap once, twice, three times, four times and five times.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>It gives seventy two, one hundred forty four, and two hundred sixteen.
Then two hundred eighty eight, and three hundred sixty degrees.

marks.gap: 360° ÷ 6 = 60° is written beside six equal arms
marks.list: the six turns are written one after the other
marks.more: the last three turns are ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>Step three, for six angles, draw six equal arms.
Three hundred sixty divided by six is sixty degrees.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Repeat the gap, and the turns are sixty, one hundred twenty, one hundred eighty.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Then two hundred forty, three hundred, and three hundred sixty degrees.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Yes: 5 equal arms 72° apart give 72°, 144°, 216°, 288°, 360°; 6 equal arms 60° apart give 60°, 120°, 180°, 240°, 300°, 360°
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Five equal arms and six equal arms both work.
Five arms are seventy two degrees apart, and six arms are sixty degrees apart.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks any five arms give five angles of symmetry, whatever the gaps.
<bookmark mark='uneven'/>Draw five arms with uneven gaps, and turn them so one arm lands on the next.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The other arms miss their places, so the gaps must be equal.
